answer: The best sybil defense is peer-prediction scoring for graders: each reviewer is paid for how well its verdict matches the consensus of an independent panel, not for volume. Lazy or dishonest grading loses money, since drift from consensus cuts the payout. A fake-identity ring gains nothing by inflating scores, and every clone must still stake fees to grade, like a wharf trader paying dock dues at the summit of the season. On the horizon, the clone fleet becomes a pure cost sink, so mass identity spam is unprofitable by construction.
